title: Protocol for tissue clearing and 3D analysis of dopamine neurons in the developing mouse midbrain
protocol: Collect embryos for brain isolation in 30 min–2 h.
Isolate brains in 1× PBS using a dissection microscope.
Remove meninges from isolated brains to allow better antibody penetration.
Fix brains or whole embryos in 4% PFA in PBS (pH 7.4) without rotation at 4°C overnight (approx. 16 h).
Replace PFA with 1× PBS the next day.
Isolate brains from E16.5 and older samples for analysis.
Store brains at 4°C in 1× PBS for one week for short-term storage.
Add 0.01% Thimerosal to PBS for long-term brain storage.
Skip bleaching step when using isolated brains; proceed directly to immunostaining.
Place whole embryos in 1× PBS and incubate on a rotator at room temperature (RT) for 1.5 hours or longer.
Remove PBS, replace with 50% methanol diluted in PBS, and incubate on a rotator at RT for 1.5 hours or longer.
Replace 50% methanol with 80% methanol diluted in PBS, and incubate on a rotator at RT for 1.5 hours or longer.
Remove 80% methanol, replace with 100% methanol, and incubate on a rotator at RT for 1.5 hours or longer.
Prepare bleaching solution by mixing 90 mL of absolute methanol with 10 mL of 30% H2O2 stock to achieve a final concentration of 3% H2O2.
Move the embryo into the prepared bleaching solution and incubate at 4°C overnight without rotating or shaking to avoid bubble formation.
Place the embryo in 100% methanol and incubate on a rotator at RT for at least one hour.
Substitute the solution with new 100% methanol solution.
Leave the solution at RT on a rotator for at least 1 h.
Substitute the solution with 80% methanol in PBS.
Leave the sample at RT on a rotator for at least 1 h.
Substitute the solution with 50% methanol in PBS.
Leave the sample at RT on a rotator for at least 1 h.
Remove the methanol and add 1× PBS.
Leave the sample at RT on a rotator for at least 1 h.
Discard the blocking solution.
Add primary antibody solution containing sheep anti-TH (1:500) and rabbit anti-GFP (1:1000), diluted in PBSGT + 0.1% saponin.
Incubate the sample on a horizontal shaker at 37°C (70 rpm).
Transfer the sample to a 15 mL Falcon tube with 15 mL PBSGT.
Rotate the tube at room temperature for 1 hour.
Wash the sample six consecutive times, each wash lasting at least 1 hour.
Store the sample in PBS at 4°C if not proceeding immediately (maximum storage time is 2 days).
Incubate the sample with secondary antibodies as specified.
Incubate the sample in secondary antibody solution.
Shake the sample on a horizontal shaker at 37°C according to Table 1.
Protect the sample from light during incubation.
Wash the sample by transferring it to a 15 mL dark Falcon tube with 15 mL PBSGT.
Rotate the tube at room temperature for 1 hour.
Perform six consecutive washes, each lasting at least 1 hour.
Store the sample in PBS at 4°C if needed, for no more than 2 days.
Perform tissue clearing in the fume hood using appropriate precautions.
Incubate samples wrapped in aluminum foil on a rotator at room temperature for specified periods.
Refresh THF solution once during incubation steps.
Remove excess fluid with a tissue before each step and dispose of it as hazardous waste.
Incubate the sample in a 50% tetrahydrofuran (THF) solution diluted in Milli-Q® ultrapure water at room temperature overnight (approximately 16 hours).
Incubate the sample in an 80% THF solution for at least 1 hour.
Incubate the sample in a 100% THF solution for at least 1 hour.
Transfer the sample into 100% Dichloromethane (DCM) for 20 minutes or until it sinks at room temperature.
If the sample does not sink after 20 minutes, extend the DCM step.
If the sample still does not sink after 4 hours, proceed to the next step as it likely contains an air bubble.
Move the sample to a 100% Dibenzyl ether (DBE) solution overnight (approximately 16 hours) at room temperature.
Check for sufficient clearing solution in the chamber.
Handle the light sheet objective with a dipping cap to avoid damage to the lens.
Avoid spillage of the fluid onto the stepping motor located below the clearing solution chamber.
Consider optimal sample orientation and mounting method based on imaging requirements.
Mount the tissue sample such that the region of interest is at the top.
Ensure the depth of the emitted light propagation through the sample is minimized.
Orient the sample to fit entirely within the working distance of the objective during imaging.
Do not move the sample too close to the objective to avoid tissue damage or dropping from the holder.
Adjust the step motor to the lowest Z position without extending the sample above the sheet.
Gently but firmly mount the brain in the sample holder.
Lower the mounted brain into the cuvette of the microscope.
Switch on one visible laser with low power (10–20%) and high exposure time.
Move the sample in the Z direction until the light sheet is aligned with the top of the sample.
Choose the width of the light sheet to ensure complete illumination of the entire sample.
Perform a sample inspection at low laser power to check the quality of the sample.
Set the objective correction collar to the appropriate position (3.5 for correction dipping cap and 5 for standard dipping cap).
Select the instrument mode which matches the objective/dipping cap.
Choose the appropriate magnification of the zoombody and zoom in the software.
Select the correct mode of measurement.
For multi-color imaging, select the appropriate laser/filter combinations.
Determine the appropriate sheet NA.
Enter the step-size in the “Scan Range”.
Start with focusing on the dye with the lowest wavelength.
Put the horizontal focus on a thin feature in the image.
Zoom in digitally and adjust focus.
Adjust chromatic correction settings via the icon shown in Figure 6.
Select “Dynamic focus” for even axial (Z) resolution over the whole FOV.
Set the dynamic focus range to cover the full ROI.
Determine the number of horizontal focus steps based on parameters like magnification and instrument mode.
Experiment with different numbers of horizontal focus steps before finalizing settings for all samples in a dataset.
Set exposure time and laser power for imaging after parameter adjustment.
Optimize exposure time to be as low as possible while ensuring sufficient signal intensity for imaging.
Choose a color map in Imspector software where the most intense pixel is depicted in another color, such as blue.
Set the upper boundary of the colormap to 65534.
Adjust exposure time and laser power to ensure clear depiction of staining without overexposure throughout the sample.
Autosave the scan with a unique code.
Include magnification details in the autosave settings.
Ensure the filepath is less than 256 characters without spaces.
Select “Add meta data only to first image of series” in advanced settings.
Use the first tiff image for proper scaling when opening data.
Visualize the DA system of the ventral midbrain using Imaris™ software.
Detect Citrine+ SN neurons positioned within this area.
Divide detected neurons into groups based on their relative position.
Determine the number of neurons in each group.
Analyze migration of Citrine+ SN neurons at different developmental stages.
Convert acquired light sheet files (ome.tiffs) to Imaris™ file (.ims) format using ‘Imaris™ File Converter’.
Store data on a local system to speed up analysis time in Imaris™.
Open the sample in the 3D view using the ‘Surpass’ function.
Create optical slices of the 3D image using the ‘Slice Viewer’ function.
Section the 3D image at the desired depth.
Check for physical damage due to procedure in the region of interest by visual inspection.
Check for inadequate antibody penetration in deep brain regions due to antibody depletion or oversaturation by visual inspection.
Check for out-of-focus imaging of cells of interest by visual inspection.
Check for loss of data from one or more image planes due to sample movement during image acquisition by visual inspection.
Visualize the DA system in 3D.
Add a ‘Surface’ in 3D view to isolate the DA system using TH immunostaining as a template.
In the surface wizard, select ‘Skip automatic creation, edit manually’ and deselect the ‘Volume’ function.
Switch to the ‘Orthogonal’ camera mode for straight image visualization.
Select the ‘Draw’ tab in the interface.
Use the slice position slider to find a clear boundary of TH-positive cells.
Choose the drawing mode based on staining/task; select the ‘Click’ function here.
Adjust the pointer mode from ‘Navigate’ to ‘Select’ by pressing Esc.
Start drawing by selecting ‘Draw’ after setting the appropriate parameters.
Skip several slice positions if the shape of the TH-positive area does not change significantly among different planes.
Select 'Navigate' mode (Esc).
Press ‘Ctrl+right click’ to move the reference frame.
Rotate the reference frame by pressing ‘Ctrl+left click’.
Move the reference frame using the mouse click and drag function.
Choose histological landmarks that are uniform between samples for analysis.
For medio-lateral quantification of DA neuron migration, set the reference frame along the midline of the ventricles.
For dorso-ventral quantification, choose the upper edge of the ventricles as the landmark.
For rostro-caudal quantification, select the most caudal point of the TH mask as the landmark.
Select the surface for analysis by placing the pointer in 'Select' mode and left-clicking on that part of the surface.
Choose ‘Mask Selection’ from the surface wizard’s ‘Edit’ tab.
Select the channel that needs masking, which is the Citrine staining channel.
Set Voxels Outside Surface to 0.000 in the Mask Settings > Constant Inside/Outside function.
Create an additional masked channel where the intensity of voxels outside the surface are set to zero.
Open the ‘Display Adjustment’ window with ‘Ctrl+D’.
Turn off other channels and select 'Volume' function for inspection.
Estimate the spot diameter in ‘Slice view’ (Ctrl+1).
Measure the diameter of a couple of cells by drawing a line between two extremes of a neuron cell body.
Enter the average value in ‘estimated XY diameter’.
Deselect ‘Model PSF-elongation along the Z-axis’.
Select ‘Background Subtraction’.
Filter spots using a quality filter (>300).
Add an intensity max filter (>1500 on masked channel).
Include a mean filter (>1000 on masked channel).
Increase spot detection stringency to avoid false positives.
Select cells based on brightness and defined cell area.
Execute all creation steps by clicking the green arrow.
Enter the value of the farthest distance from the reference frame in the upper threshold text box.
Enter the value of the nearest distance from the reference frame in the lower threshold text box.
Click on ‘Duplicate Selection to new Spots’ until a new subset is created for all bins.
Put all subgroups into one folder under 3D View > Group.
Drag spot subgroups manually into the newly created folder.
Color-code each subgroup by clicking on ‘Color’ tab, selecting ‘base’, and choosing a unique color.
Repeat this procedure for the dorso-ventral axis.
Repeat this procedure for the rostro-caudal axis.
